key_insight: AgentFairBench is a benchmark designed to measure whether LLM agents show demographic bias in the actions they take, not just in the answers they generate.
clinical_relevance: For medical triage and other decision-making settings, it provides a way to check whether agentic AI treats demographic groups differently when recommending actions.
method: Counterfactual matched profiles vary only by a name-coded race × gender signal across hiring, lending, and medical triage.
Four agent setups are tested: direct, chain-of-thought, multi-agent deliberation, and tool-augmented.
The harness reports counterfactual flip rate, MASD, action-rate disparity, and tool-invocation disparity with bootstrap CIs and statistical correction.
evidence_signal: In the pilot evaluation (864 decisions plus replication), no demographic effect was detected for claude haiku 4.5 after arity-matched testing and multiple-comparison correction, while a planted-bias test showed the benchmark can detect disparity when it exists.
watch_item: Results depend on synthetic benchmark setups and model/configuration choices, so real-world deployment still needs local validation and careful interpretation.
paper_title: AgentFairBench: Do LLM Agents Discriminate When They Act?
